Humble Spring Sale, Day 12 (Tuesday)

For the twelfth day of the spring sale there are a ton of new sales. I'm not going to cover all the games on sale, since they have a ton, but I'll pick some that I feel strongly about from each day.

Ether One
This game is unique because you can actually skip the puzzles and turn it into a pure walking simulator if you want to. I wouldn't really recommend that, it would be super short and not very satisfying - the puzzles provide a lot of the story - but if you just want to collect a few red ribbons you can do that.

The puzzles are pretty decent, and do require a thorough exploration of the neat-looking levels - the things and information you need are not necessarily right next together.

 

Back To Bed
A puzzle game based around controlling the path of a sleepwalking man who only goes straight, and turns right when he bumps into things.

The hard-mode puzzles in this game are actually pretty good - but you do have to spend about an hour beating the easy puzzles before that unlocks. It could also use a rewind button, so if you make a mistake you don't have to redo all the actions on a complicated puzzle.

 

Insanely Twisted Shadow Planet
Even though this game wasn't particularly challenging it was really nice to look at - and satisfying to play. Zipping around in your little flying saucer, using your tools to manipulate the environment was unique. I might almost call it more of an experience, although that wouldn't really be fair to the sedate but interesting design.

 

140
I quite enjoyed this little abstract platformer, although it is super short (under an hour if I remember correctly). For $0.99 it might be worth giving a shot though - there's also a hardcore mode after you finish - playing all the levels backwards.

 

SteamWorld Dig
This was a few hours of solid gameplay, although the only thing I found particularly exciting was the final boss fight - which was excellent. The rest of the game was pretty good, but mining gems to buy more equipment and fighting a few enemies probably won't thrill most people. The design was good, it just wasn't particularly challenging.

 

Survivor Squad
An interesting premise and gameplay, that was ultimately ruined by some quirky design decisions.

The main problem was that after playing for hours, if you fail one mission you can totally screw your game - and it won't let you replay that mission. However if you're about to lose your last guy you CAN replay - but this will almost always be too late for a replay to actually save you. Some of the looting and trade mechanics had similarly flawed logic.

 

QuestRun
While it has a relatively low resolution, this is a pretty decent and very challenging turn-based combat game. You have to balance your party in a strange way to actually win, and the missions are very long - but I liked it as a difficult experience.

I do wish they gave you some good pets when you start out though, since pets are so crucial to survival - it takes too long to unlock those. (or they could just give a difficulty setting so you could tone down the damage a bit)

 

BardBarian
A party based shooter that gives you far too large of a hitbox, and has an emphasis on repeating levels over and over. This got pretty boring fast, and there isn't any way around it since you have to grind for upgrades or you physically don't have enough damage to beat later levels.

 

Solar Flux
This space puzzle-game is incredibly tightly tuned, getting three stars requires being very precise, and there isn't much difference between the two and three star ratings - so you'll probably either get 1 or 3 stars. The problem is that you need a ton of 3 star ratings to unlock later levels, so just accepting a low score isn't an option.

 

Sang Froid
I wanted to get into this game, because people I know have enjoyed it, but the tutorials are so long and wordy. The narrator droning on in his soothing voice almost put me to sleep. Maybe if it was interactive, rather than video-tutorial it would have been better.

That's a shame because the intro story seemed interesting, they just threw way too much non-game content at you in the beginning.

 

Teslagrad
This cute puzzle platformer has an interesting story, though it's mostly told to you through context as well as the murals constructed from the collectibles throughout the game. These are sometimes quite difficult to reach - so you may not get all of them your first playthrough. Some of the boss fights can be tough, but it's an interesting little game if you like platformers.

 

Risk of Rain
The concept is solid but this game has a lot of technical issues, even if you aren't recording. If you are trying to record it's even worse since it doesn't play well with FRAPS or Dxtory (though I've heard that OBS sometimes works). It's a fun co-op experience, mowing down waves of monsters, grabbing loot and upgrades for your character - but the lag when the game gets busier can ruin this.

 

Metal Dead
This point-and-click has a weird and wacky sense of humor, and it wasn't really my type of game. I also remember the resolution being pretty low, and obviously the graphics have a rough hand-drawn quality. Feels more flash game than polished release to me.

 

Saints Row 4
If you liked Saints Row 3 you'll probably enjoy this one - it's more of the same over-the-top action, but this time you also have superhero powers. Cars and planes are almost obsolete since you can run faster and fly on your own, and this makes getting around much more pleasant. Really it has every activity and character the previous game had, rebranded differently, but has a more comic book flavor.

Oh and the title intro to this game is absolutely fantastic.

It seems pretty obvious that season 2 is significantly worse than season 1. Karen has regressed as a character, the backstage workings are overshadowed by drama, dialogue is bad – the whole thing is just a train wreck.

That said, how would you have changed season 2 so that it didn't suck. Personally, I would have:

  • Kept Frank and possibly Dev.
  • Drop Frank's cheating plot, i.e. the poorly written excuse to get rid of him.
  • Reduce the roles of Jimmy and Kyle.
  • DON'T KILL OFF KYLE. Or try to create a Rent knock-off.
  • Not send Hit List to Broadway or the Tony Awards.
  • Get rid of or reduce the role of Ana.
  • Drop Ivy's pregnancy plot line.
  • Drop Jimmy's dark past stuff.
  • Make Jimmy's arc about realistic expectations for his new show and the realization that his first piece of writing is not a masterpiece.
  • Flesh out the plot of Hit List and make it more apparent in the show.
  • Have the pilot start right after the events of the season 1 finale and address Ivy's suicide attempt first rather than addressing it in an offhand comment.

There are some other ideas, but those are the main ones.
